newsitem.title: USA: MCI appointments ahead of BT merger.
newsitem.headline: MCI appointments ahead of BT merger.

text.p: MCI said on Thursday that chairman Bert Roberts will immediately assume direct responsibility for the integration planning of international activities of British Telecommunications Plc and MCI.
After the closing of the merger between the two companies, Roberts will become co-chairman of the new company, known as Concert, along with Sir Iain Vallance, who is now chairman of BT.
The company also said that Gerald Taylor, who will be chief executive officer of MCI until the merger is completed, will direct transition planning for the two companies.
After the closing of the merger, Taylor becomes president and chief operating office of the new Concert.
It also said that Timothy Price, who will be president and chief operating officer of MCI after the merger, is named to that position effective immediately.
MCI said the company will operate as an autonomous wholly-owned subsidiary of Concert.

"I am executing this important succession plan today in anticipation of the MCI-BT merger," Roberts said in a statement. "Moving seasoned executives into key positions clearly reflects the strength and depth of MCI management."
"We can now execute this merger flawlessly and, at the same time, achieve our current operating goals. We will do all this without missing a beat," he said.
Roberts was named MCI chairman and CEO in 1992, after serving as president and chief operating officer since 1985.
Taylor joined MCI in 1969 shortly after its founding and was elected to his current position in 1994. As part of the recent merger announcement, Taylor was named to the BT board of directors.
Price joined MCI in 1984 and has held his current position since 1995.
Concert will be headquartered in both London and Washington, D.C. The two companies announced the merger on November 3 and have said they expect approval by the fall of 1997.
